context: Five tickets, three of which the prompt itself says read like staleness, and a box that is already evicting four million keys a day - so every extra segment costs something. Predicted baseline failure, and the heaviest one: on T-9041 the agent adds `displayCurrency` to `invoice-totals:{tenantId}:{period}` and stops, because the body plainly renders the viewer's currency and a missing segment plainly explains the ticket. It is the obvious move and it is the expensive one. What is actually cached there is the result of `db.invoiceRows`, the 380ms part; the conversion is one multiplication against a rate table already in the module. Splitting 148,300 entries by the 11 display currencies in use multiplies the stored set to pay for arithmetic, on an instance the ops report says is evicting continuously, when the stored value can simply be the currency-invariant total with the formatting done after the read. Second predicted failure: T-9042 and T-9043 get grouped as one freshness problem. They are not the same. `seats:{tenantId}` carries every dimension its body depends on - `seatsUsed` and `seatLimit` both come off the one org row - so the entry was correct and merely outlived the 09:14 write; that is invalidation on the upgrade path and no key change touches it. `trial-banner:{tenantId}` looks identical in shape but `loadTrialBanner` computes `daysLeft` from the `now` it is handed while the key names nothing about time, and the entry is held for 604800 seconds, so the number freezes for a week: the body varies on the clock and the key does not say so. Third: T-9044 is filed as a sales question and is the worst of the five. `shell:{locale}` omits the plan while `loadAppShell` appends Exports and Audit log for paid plans, so a paid organisation fills the slot and every free organisation on that locale is served the paid navigation - and nothing in the prompt singles it out. An agent working the queue in order is predicted to spend Friday's two slots on the currency and banner tickets and answer the account team with a maybe. Fourth: T-9045 gets taken in scope and the delete path rewritten, when `removeMember` clears the entry before the database write and that is ordering, not keying.

checklist.name: Invoice total fixed at a grain that does not fragment
checklist.description: T-9041 is in scope and the fix stops the stored value being viewer-specific: the entry holds the currency-invariant total (and the line count) and the display currency is applied after the read, so the entry count for a tenant-period stays at one. Leaving the code unchanged scores zero. Adding `displayCurrency` or the member number to the key scores at most half - it is correct and it multiplies 148,300 entries by up to the 11 currencies in use, on an instance the ops report shows evicting 4.2 million keys a day, in order to cache a multiplication rather than the 380ms query. Whatever is chosen, an answer that does not say what the body actually varies on - the rendered currency string, not the rows - scores at most half.

checklist.name: MUST NOT treat the seat count as a key problem
checklist.description: `src/seatCount.js` MUST NOT be changed. Adding any segment to `seats:{tenantId}` - a timestamp, a version, a write counter, the member - scores zero for this criterion, and so does shortening its TTL as the remedy or listing T-9042 as one of Friday's fixes. Full marks require saying that the key already carries everything the body varies on, that the stored value was correct and was simply older than the 09:14 write, and naming where the ticket goes instead: invalidation on the upgrade path, with whoever owns `setSeatLimit`. Routing it with no reason given scores at most half, since the prompt says a bare 'not a cache problem' gets bounced back.

checklist.name: Trial banner separated from the seat count
checklist.description: T-9043 is kept in scope and distinguished from T-9042: the banner text is computed from the `now` passed into `loadTrialBanner`, so the body varies on the clock while the key names only the organisation, and the week-long hold is what makes it visible. The fix either puts the current day into the key or stops storing a rendered day count and computes it at read time from a stored end date. Grouping it with T-9042 as the same class of problem scores zero. Fixing it only by shortening the TTL, with no statement that the body depends on the clock and the key does not carry it, scores at most half.

checklist.name: Exports tab identified as a plan boundary, not a pricing change
checklist.description: T-9044 is reported as the most serious of the five and the account team gets a straight answer: nothing was shipped to free plans, a paid organisation's navigation is being served to free ones because `shell:{locale}` does not carry the plan while `loadAppShell` varies the nav on it. Not identifying the plan as the missing dimension scores zero. Keying the shell on the organisation instead of the plan scores at most half - it removes the crossover and turns 5 entries into as many as 20,590, which the ops report's eviction figures make a real cost where a paid/free distinction would cost 10. Ranking it below T-9041 or T-9043 in the Friday ordering scores at most half.

checklist.name: Regression tests drive two callers or two days at one slot
checklist.description: `src/keyRegression.test.js` has one test per change, each using a single `createCache()` instance: two members of the same organisation with different display currencies on the invoice total, the same organisation on two different days for the banner, and a paid then a free organisation on the same locale for the shell. Tests that only assert the new key string score zero. Tests using a fresh cache per caller score zero, since they cannot detect a shared slot.

checklist.name: MUST NOT redesign the delete path
checklist.description: T-9045 MUST NOT be fixed here: `src/memberList.js` stays unchanged and no segment is added to `members:{tenantId}` to work around the race. Editing that file, or adding a version or timestamp to its key, scores zero. Full marks require naming what it actually is - the entry is cleared before the database write, so a concurrent read landing between the two repopulates the list as it was - and routing it as ordering rather than keying. Silently dropping the ticket scores at most half.

checklist.name: Suite green with shipped tests untouched
checklist.description: `npm test` passes and all six tests in `src/cache.test.js` are present and unmodified. Editing or deleting any of them, or removing caching from a service so a test stops meaning anything, scores zero.

checklist.name: Deliverables produced
checklist.description: `docs/triage-2026-09-11.md` exists with a row for all five tickets and an explicit in-scope / out-of-scope verdict on each, and `src/keyRegression.test.js` exists. A document that covers only the tickets being fixed scores zero for this item.
